claim: Injectisomes are multi-protein transmembrane machines allowing pathogenic bacteria to inject effector proteins into eukaryotic host cells, a process called type III secretion.
source: Injectisomes are multi-protein transmembrane machines allowing pathogenic bacteria to inject effector proteins into eukaryotic host cells, a process called type III secretion.
evidence: This is a definitional statement supported by established scientific knowledge about type III secretion systems.

claim: Basal bodies of injectisomes inside the bacterial cells showed length variations of 20%.
source: Unexpectedly, basal bodies of injectisomes inside the bacterial cells showed length variations of 20%.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements from cryo-ET imaging and MRA classification showing intermembrane distances ranging from 30 to 36 nm.

claim: The in situ structures of the Y. enterocolitica and S. flexneri injectisomes had similar dimensions and were significantly longer than the isolated structures of related injectisomes.
source: The in situ structures of the Y. enterocolitica and S. flexneri injectisomes had similar dimensions and were significantly longer than the isolated structures of related injectisomes.
evidence: This is supported by direct comparison of cryo-ET measurements showing ~33 nm intermembrane distance in situ versus ~20 nm for isolated structures.

claim: The crystal structure of the inner membrane injectisome component YscD appeared elongated compared to a homologous protein.
source: The crystal structure of the inner membrane injectisome component YscD appeared elongated compared to a homologous protein, and molecular dynamics simulations documented its elongation elasticity.
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data at 2.7 Å and 1.4 Å resolution showing YscD in an extended conformation compared to PrgH.

claim: Molecular dynamics simulations documented the elongation elasticity of YscD.
source: The crystal structure of the inner membrane injectisome component YscD appeared elongated compared to a homologous protein, and molecular dynamics simulations documented its elongation elasticity.
evidence: This is supported by steered MD simulations showing YscD can undergo 3.5 nm elongation while opposing forces of 35 ± 15 pN.

claim: The ring-shaped secretin YscC at the outer membrane was stretched by 30–40% in situ, compared to its isolated liposome-embedded conformation.
source: The ring-shaped secretin YscC at the outer membrane was stretched by 30–40% in situ, compared to its isolated liposome-embedded conformation.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of cryo-ET structures of isolated YscC in liposomes versus in situ injectisomes.

claim: Elasticity is critical for some two-membrane spanning protein complexes to cope with variations in the intermembrane distance.
source: We suggest that elasticity is critical for some two-membrane spanning protein complexes to cope with variations in the intermembrane distance.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed structural flexibility and osmotic stress experiments.

claim: The assembly of the injectisome involves some 34 different proteins.
source: The assembly of the injectisome involves some 34 different proteins.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge about injectisome composition.

claim: Phylogenic analyses based on the most conserved proteins classify injectisomes into seven different families (Ysc, Ssa-Esc, Inv-Mxi-Spa, Hrc1, Hrc2, Rhizobiales, and Chlamydiales).
source: Phylogenic analyses based on the most conserved proteins classify injectisomes into seven different families (Ysc, Ssa-Esc, Inv-Mxi-Spa, Hrc1, Hrc2, Rhizobiales, and Chlamydiales) (Pallen et al., 2005; Troisfontaines and Cornelis, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by cited phylogenetic studies.

claim: The injectisome consists of three parts: a ∼60 nm long, hollow needle protruding from the bacterial surface, a basal body that spans the two bacterial membranes and the periplasm, and a cytoplasmic part.
source: The injectisome consists of three parts: a ∼60 nm long, hollow needle protruding from the bacterial surface, a basal body that spans the two bacterial membranes and the periplasm, and a cytoplasmic part.
evidence: This is supported by established structural knowledge of injectisomes.

claim: The barrel-shaped structure spanning the OM and protruding into the periplasm consists of a 12–15 mer of a protein from the secretin family (YscC, InvG, MxiD).
source: The barrel-shaped structure spanning the OM and protruding into the periplasm consists of a 12–15 mer of a protein from the secretin family (YscC, InvG, MxiD) (Burghout et al., 2004; Marlovits et al., 2004; Hodgkinson et al., 2009; Spreter et al., 2009; Schraidt and Marlovits, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited structural studies on secretin proteins.

claim: The lower double-ring reaching into the IM is made of a lipoprotein (YscJ, PrgK, MxiJ) proposed to form a 24-subunit ring.
source: The lower double-ring reaching into the IM is made of a lipoprotein (YscJ, PrgK, MxiJ) proposed to form a 24-subunit ring (Kimbrough and Miller, 2000; Crepin et al., 2005; Yip et al., 2005; Silva-Herzog et al., 2008; Hodgkinson et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by cited structural and biochemical studies.

claim: The injectisome is evolutionarily related to the bacterial flagellar motor system, with which it shares the basic type III secretion export apparatus.
source: The injectisome is evolutionarily related to the bacterial flagellar motor system, with which it shares the basic type III secretion export apparatus (Cornelis, 2006; Minamino et al., 2008; Erhardt et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by cited evolutionary and structural studies.

claim: The Y. enterocolitica injectisome structure was obtained at ∼4 nm resolution using cryo electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging.
source: This yielded a reconstruction of the injectisome in situ at ∼4 nm resolution (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by FSC analysis showing resolution of 4 nm by the gold standard criterion.

claim: The vertical distance between the centers of the membranes in the Y. enterocolitica injectisome reconstruction is ∼33 nm.
source: The vertical distance between the centers of the membranes in the reconstruction is ∼33 nm.
evidence: This is directly measured from the cryo-ET reconstruction.

claim: The average intermembrane distance of ∼33 nm is significantly larger than the ∼20 nm expected from the structures of basal bodies isolated from Salmonella enterica SPI-I and S. flexneri.
source: This average value is in the range of values reported for gram-negative bacteria (Chen et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2012), but significantly larger than the ∼20 nm expected from the structures of basal bodies isolated from Salmonella enterica SPI-I and S. flexneri (Hodgkinson et al., 2009; Schraidt and Marlovits, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published structures and independent CEMOVIS measurements.

claim: The largest lateral diameter of the periplasmic part of the average injectisome structure is 18 nm.
source: Measuring from mass center to mass center, the largest lateral diameter of the periplasmic part of the average injectisome structure is 18 nm (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is measured from the cryo-ET reconstruction.

claim: The largest diameter at the outer OM is 12 nm.
source: The largest diameter at the outer OM is 12 nm (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), which is in good agreement with the dimensions of isolated and liposome reconstituted YscC complexes (see below).
evidence: This is measured from the cryo-ET reconstruction and compared with isolated YscC structures.

claim: A large ring-like structure can be discerned on the cytoplasmic side of the IM.
source: Further, a large ring-like structure can be discerned on the cytoplasmic side of the IM (Figure 2A, yellow).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-ET reconstruction.

claim: A smaller, torus-like structure localized ∼5 nm underneath the membrane is tentatively proposed to be the export gate YscV.
source: It surrounds a smaller, torus-like structure localized ∼5 nm underneath the membrane, which we tentatively propose to be the export gate YscV (Figure 2A, red), based on the localization of the export gate protein FlhA of the flagella motor (Abrusci et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with the flagellar motor system structure.

claim: Intermembrane distances in individual Y. enterocolitica injectisomes ranged from 30 to 36 nm.
source: Classification by iterative multi reference alignment (MRA) of individual in situ Y. enterocolitica injectisomes revealed large variations in the length of the complex in the intermembrane space; intermembrane distances ranged from 30 to 36 nm (Figure 2B–C)
evidence: This is determined by MRA classification of sub-tomogram data.

claim: The crystal structure of YscD150–362 was determined at 2.7 Å resolution.
source: The 2.7 Å resolution structure of YscD150–362 (Supplementary file 1A) showed three linearly arranged domains (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data collection and refinement.

claim: YscD150–362 showed three linearly arranged domains, each comprising an αββαβ-ring building motif.
source: The 2.7 Å resolution structure of YscD150–362 (Supplementary file 1A) showed three linearly arranged domains (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1). Each domain comprises an αββαβ-ring building motif
evidence: This is determined from the crystal structure.

claim: YscD features an extended conformation, while the domains of PrgH are in a more compact arrangement.
source: However, although sharing the same multi-domain architecture, YscD features an extended conformation, while the domains of PrgH are in a more compact arrangement.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison of YscD and PrgH crystal structures.

claim: Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the connecting hinge (residues A282-N284) between the second and third periplasmic domains is mainly responsible for the high flexibility of YscD.
source: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that the connecting hinge (residues A282-N284) between the second and third periplasmic domains is mainly responsible for the high flexibility of YscD (Figure 3—figure supplement 2, 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is determined from MD simulations and normal mode analysis.

claim: The G283P mutation resulted in a protein that was still functional for type III secretion in vivo.
source: Mutation of G283 to a proline resulted in a protein that was still functional for type III secretion in vivo (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by secretion assays showing complementation of the ΔyscD strain.

claim: The crystal structure of YscD150–347 G283P was determined at 1.4 Å resolution.
source: The 1.4 Å resolution crystal structure of YscD150–347 G283P had a slightly more bent conformation in the hinge region
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data collection and refinement.

claim: The periplasmic domains of YscD can undergo a maximal elongation of about 3.5 nm.
source: Due to this tertiary structure elasticity, that is, the rearrangement of tertiary structure in response to mechanical force, the periplasmic domains of YscD can undergo a maximal elongation of about 3.5 nm (i.e., a 50% elongation compared to the compact conformation)
evidence: This is determined from steered molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: YscD opposes stretching with a force as small as 35 ± 15 pN per YscD monomer.
source: while opposing the stretching with a force as small as 35 ± 15 pN per YscD monomer, a value that is comparable with that estimated for other highly stretchable multi-domain proteins (Hsin and Schulten, 2011).
evidence: This is calculated from steered MD simulations.

claim: A pseudo-atomic model of the inner membrane part of the basal body was constructed by combining experimental data with molecular modeling and simulations.
source: We constructed a pseudo-atomic model of the inner membrane part of the basal body by combining experimental data with molecular modeling and simulations, similar as to exercised previously to unveil the architecture of large macromolecular complexes (Alber et al., 2007; Lasker et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by the integration of cryo-ET, crystallography, and computational modeling data.

claim: The YscDJ ring model is a 24-mer assembly.
source: Multimers of the YscD and the YscJ proteins were assembled into symmetrical 24-meric ring models using a newly developed optimization protocol based on swarm intelligence heuristic method (Degiacomi and Dal Peraro, 2013).
evidence: This is determined by computational modeling constrained by cryo-ET and cross-linking data.

claim: The S. flexneri injectisome was reconstructed at ∼7 nm resolution.
source: We examined Shigella flexneri bacteria by cryo-ET and generated an average in situ structure of the Shigella flexneri injectisome (Figure 5) at ∼7 nm resolution.
evidence: This is determined by FSC analysis of the cryo-ET reconstruction.

claim: The intermembrane distance in the S. flexneri injectisome is 32 nm.
source: Nevertheless, despite the lower resolution, the map allows to reliably detect the positions of the membrane surrounding the injectisome, resulting in a length measurement between the centers of the membranes of 32 nm (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is measured from the cryo-ET reconstruction.

claim: The isolated and liposome-inserted YscC complexes were reconstructed at a resolution of ∼3 nm.
source: To evaluate the contribution of the secretin YscC to the elasticity, we expressed and purified full-length YscC, reconstituted it into liposomes, and reconstructed its structure at a resolution of ∼3 nm by cryo-ET and sub-volume averaging (Figure 6).
evidence: This is determined by cryo-ET and sub-volume averaging.

claim: YscC undergoes a 30–40% length extension in the assembled injectisome compared to its lipid vesicle-reconstituted state.
source: The described assignment of the YscC/YscD junction would correspond to a 30–40% length extension of YscC in the assembled injectisome, with respect to its lipid vesicle-reconstituted state (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is determined by comparison of cryo-ET structures of isolated versus in situ YscC.

claim: The isolated S. flexneri injectisome would have to be stretched by ∼40% to match the dimensions of the average in situ Yersinia structure.
source: Even the shortest of our MRA class averages of in situ Yersinia injectisomes (Figure 2B) is still longer than the isolated Shigella injectisome, which would have to be stretched by ∼40% to match the dimensions of the average in situ Yersinia structure (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is determined by comparison of in situ and isolated structures.

claim: Exposure of Y. enterocolitica bacteria to osmotic stress from high salt conditions resulted in a significant elongation of their basal bodies.
source: This is supported by our finding that exposure of the Y. enterocolitica bacteria to osmotic stress from high salt conditions resulted in a significant elongation of their basal bodies (Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by cryo-ET measurements of bacteria in 10× PBS showing ~10% increase in basal body length.

claim: The length of observed basal bodies increased by ∼10% under high salt conditions.
source: The length of observed basal bodies increased by ∼10% (with statistical significance, Figure 7)
evidence: This is measured from cryo-ET of bacteria in 10× PBS with statistical analysis showing p=0.05 and p=0.02.

claim: The in situ reconstructions of the Yersinia and Shigella injectisomes show high overall similarity.
source: The in situ reconstructions of the Yersinia and Shigella injectisomes show high overall similarity considering the lower resolution of the Shigella injectisome: the overall dimensions, ring hierarchy and the peptidoglycan attachment location are conserved.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the two cryo-ET reconstructions.

claim: In the Yersinia injectisome, the torus ring assigned to YscV was ∼5 nm below the membrane, while in the Shigella injectisome it was ∼10 nm below the membrane.
source: We could detect a significant difference in the location of the torus ring assigned to the N-terminus or YscV/MxiA (Abrusci et al., 2013). In the Yersinia injectisome, it was ∼5 nm below the membrane, while in the Shigella injectisome it was ∼10 nm below the membrane.
evidence: This is measured from the cryo-ET reconstructions of both species.

claim: The in situ reconstructions of the Yersinia and Shigella injectisomes did not reveal obvious C-rings.
source: However, the in situ reconstructions of the Yersinia and Shigella injectisomes did not reveal obvious C-rings (Figure 2A,B and Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-ET reconstructions.

claim: The Shigella injectisome in situ appeared about 10 nm or ∼40% longer (32 nm vs 22 nm at the membrane level) than isolated structures.
source: In addition to the observed length variations, the injectisome's basal bodies were longer in the native context than suggested from single particle structures: the Shigella injectisome in situ appeared about 10 nm or ∼40% longer (32 nm vs 22 nm at the membrane level).
evidence: This is based on comparison of in situ cryo-ET with published isolated structures.

claim: Stretching of YscC by an estimated 5 nm and an elongation of YscD by an estimated 3.5 nm would explain an ∼8.5 nm overall extension of the Yersinia injectisome's basal body.
source: Stretching of YscC by an estimated 5 nm and an elongation of YscD by an estimated 3.5 nm would explain an ∼8.5 nm overall extension of the Yersinia injectisome's basal body
evidence: This is calculated from the individual contributions of YscC and YscD elongation.

claim: Elasticity might allow the injectisome to better cope with membrane stresses.
source: We hypothesize that the here observed elasticity might allow the injectisome to better cope with such membrane stresses.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed structural flexibility and osmotic stress experiments.

claim: The basal bodies of bacterial flagellar motors do not seem to differ in dimensions between their isolated and in situ structures.
source: Furthermore, the basal bodies of the bacterial flagellar motors do not seem to differ in dimensions between their isolated and in situ structures (Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on comparison with published flagellar motor structures.

claim: For more fragile protein complexes that span two membranes, tertiary structure elasticity may constitute a general mechanism for structural protection.
source: We here hypothesize that for more fragile protein complexes that span two membranes, tertiary structure elasticity may constitute a general mechanism for structural protection.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the findings from this study.

claim: Y. enterocolitica minicells were genetically engineered and still had assembled injectisomes.
source: Since thick cells reduced the quality of tomographic imaging, we genetically engineered Y. enterocolitica minicells that were thinner and still had assembled injectisomes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy and cryo-ET imaging showing injectisomes in minicells.

claim: The channel of the injectisome's needle is resolved at the OM.
source: The channel of the injectisome's needle is resolved at the OM.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-ET reconstruction.

claim: The density below the export gate likely corresponds to the YscN ATPase.
source: Similarly, in analogy to the flagellar motor system (Chen et al., 2011), the density below the export gate likely corresponds to the YscN ATPase.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with the flagellar motor system.

claim: The YscC-D junction is distinguishable in the density map.
source: The YscC-D junction is distinguishable in the density map and indicated in the density assignment (Figure 2A, asterisk).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-ET reconstruction.

claim: CEMOVIS yielded an average inter-membrane distance of 35 nm measured between the centres of electron density.
source: CEMOVIS yielded an average inter-membrane distance of 35 nm measured between the centres of electron density (Figure 2—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is measured from CEMOVIS images.

claim: The isolated YscC complexes showed several ring densities: in the membrane bilayer, ∼5.5 nm below the membrane, and ∼12 nm below the membrane.
source: The isolated and liposome-inserted YscC complexes showed several ring densities: in the membrane bilayer, ∼5.5 nm below the membrane, and ∼12 nm below the membrane.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-ET reconstruction of isolated YscC.

claim: Most of the YscD/YscJ interactions occur between the first periplasmic domain of YscD and the C-terminal domain of YscJ.
source: Most of the YscD/YscJ interactions occur between the first periplasmic domain of YscD and the C-terminal domain of YscJ.
evidence: This is determined from the computational modeling of the YscDJ ring.

claim: Only an elongated arrangement of the C-terminal periplasmic domain of YscD best fits the in situ cryo-ET map.
source: The assembly of the YscDJ ring (Figure 4) revealed that only an elongated arrangement of the C-terminal periplasmic domain of YscD—similar to the X-ray structure—best fits the in situ cryo-ET map
evidence: This is determined by fitting the atomistic model to the cryo-ET map.

claim: The fourth periplasmic domain of YscD mediates the interaction with YscC.
source: YscD is known to have four periplasmic domains. The first three are thought to form a ring structure in analogy to homologues (Spreter et al., 2009), while the fourth domain mediates the interaction with YscC (Ross and Plano, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited studies on YscD-YscC interactions.

claim: The secretin YscC was assumed inserted into the outer membrane.
source: the main components of the basal body were assigned as YscC and YscDJ rings following this nomenclature (Figure 2A) and the secretin YscC was assumed inserted into the outer membrane.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of secretin localization.

claim: The large ring-like structure on the cytoplasmic side of the IM is 21 nm wide.
source: The large ring-like structure on the cytoplasmic side of the IM is 21 nm wide.
evidence: This is measured from the cryo-ET reconstruction.

claim: The smaller, ring-like structure proposed to be the export apparatus is 11 nm wide and ∼6 nm high.
source: The smaller, ring-like structure proposed to be the export apparatus, is 11 nm wide and ∼6 nm high.
evidence: This is measured from the cryo-ET reconstruction.

claim: Each domain of YscD comprises an αββαβ-ring building motif, which superposes well with corresponding motifs in the three domains of the homologous PrgH.
source: Each domain comprises an αββαβ-ring building motif, which superposes well with corresponding motifs in the three domains of the homologous PrgH from Salmonella enterica (Spreter et al., 2009) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is determined by structural comparison of YscD and PrgH.

claim: The YscD structure points to a high inter-domain flexibility.
source: The YscD structure points to a high inter-domain flexibility, as already indicated by the high B-factor values of the third domain of wt YscD150–362 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic B-factors and MD simulations.

claim: The proline mutant has lower atomic B-factors and hence a more rigid, but still functional, structure.
source: Comparison of the dynamic mobility of each structure corroborated this; the proline mutant has lower atomic B-factors and hence a more rigid, but still functional, structure (Figure 3—figure supplement 3 and 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic B-factors and functional assays.

claim: The wt domains of YscD, as well as YscD150–347 G283P, can be arranged in a compact form similar to the corresponding region of the YscD homologue PrgH.
source: We found that the wt domains, as well as YscD150–347 G283P, can be arranged in a compact form similar to the corresponding region of the YscD homologue PrgH from Salmonella SPI-1 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is determined from MD simulations.

claim: The application of stretching forces in MD produced an almost barrier-free transition from the compact to the extended conformation.
source: Moreover, the application of stretching forces in MD produced an almost barrier-free transition from the compact to the extended conformation, resulting in a domain arrangement similar to that observed by X-ray crystallography.
evidence: This is determined from steered MD simulations.

claim: The tertiary structural elasticity of the ring components of the periplasmic portion of YscD significantly contributes to the overall elasticity of the basal body of the injectisome.
source: This suggests that the tertiary structural elasticity of the ring components of the periplasmic portion of YscD significantly contributes to the overall elasticity of the basal body of the injectisome in response to external forces.
evidence: This is an inference based on MD simulation results.

claim: The TM domain of YscD was modeled as an α-helix and equilibrated in a membrane bilayer using MD.
source: In particular, the TM domain of YscD was modeled as an α-helix and equilibrated in a membrane bilayer using MD; it connects the two ring densities of YscD on both sides of the IM without any structural strain.
evidence: This is determined from molecular modeling and MD simulations.

claim: The cytosolic domain of the YscD was modeled on the basis of the X-ray structure of the Y. pestis homologue.
source: The cytosolic domain of the YscD was modeled on the basis of the X-ray structure of the Y. pestis homologue (Lountos et al., 2012)
evidence: This is based on homology modeling using a published structure.

claim: The cryo-ET map revealed the height of the periplasmic domains of YscD and provided a hint for the radius of the ring and thus multimerization state of YscDJ.
source: The cryo-ET map did not allow a direct density fit in the radial direction, due to the limited resolution of the map; the density corresponding to YscJ was smeared. However, the map revealed the height of the periplasmic domains of YscD and provided a hint for the radius or the ring and thus multimerization state of YscDJ.
evidence: This is determined from analysis of the cryo-ET map.

claim: The limiting factor for the resolution of the S. flexneri injectisome structure was the extreme thickness of the bacteria.
source: The limiting factor for the resolution was the extreme thickness of the bacteria.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the technical limitations of imaging thick cells.

claim: A lower resolution does not affect the visible inter-membrane distance measurement.
source: This distance measurement was not affected by the resolution of the map (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by applying resolution limitation to a single particle map.

claim: Most of the YscC proteins in liposomes were facing outside of the lipid vesicles.
source: Cryo-EM imaging (see below) showed that most of the proteins were facing outside of the lipid vesicles.
evidence: This is observed from cryo-EM imaging of reconstituted YscC.

claim: The fourth periplasmic domain of YscD of 70 aa might affect the length of the YscD structure by 1–3 nm.
source: We speculate that this density corresponds to the YscC–YscD junction and also contains the fourth periplasmic domain of YscD of 70 aa, which might affect the length of the YscD structure by 1–3 nm, depending on the type of molecular interaction between YscC and YscD.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the size of the missing domain.

claim: The remaining 1.5 nm towards the observed 10 nm elongation of the Shigella system may be attributed to inter-species differences, or the limited resolution of the maps.
source: the remaining 1.5 nm towards the observed 10 nm elongation of the Shigella system may be attributed to inter-species differences, or the limited resolution of the maps.
evidence: This is a speculation about the source of the remaining difference.

claim: The distance between the export gate and the ATPases were 11–13 nm for all three assemblies (Yersinia, Shigella injectisomes, and flagellar motor).
source: The distance between the export gate and the ATPases were 11–13 nm for all three assemblies.
evidence: This is measured from the cryo-ET reconstructions and comparison with flagellar motor structures.

claim: Injectisomes contain proteins homologous to FliN and FliM, termed YscQ in Yersinia and Spa33 in Shigella, which are suggested to form a C-ring similar to bacterial flagellar motors.
source: Injectisomes contain proteins homologous to FliN and FliM, termed YscQ in Yersinia and Spa33 in Shigella, which are suggested to form a C-ring (Morita-Ishihara et al., 2006) similar to bacterial flagellar motors.
evidence: This is based on sequence homology and cited studies.

claim: YscQ could be unstructured, or being only transiently associated with the injectisome.
source: This could be caused by YscQ being unstructured, or being only transiently associated with the injectisome.
evidence: This is a speculation to explain the absence of C-ring density.

claim: The elongation of the Yersinia injectisome's basal body seems anisotropic with higher contribution from the secretin YscC.
source: The elongation of the Yersinia injectisome's basal body seems anisotropic with higher contribution from the secretin YscC, based on cryo-ET studies of isolated and membrane-reconstituted YscC.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of isolated YscC and in situ structures.

claim: A higher-resolution structure of the membrane domains of the secretins in combination with further molecular simulations may allow a full mechanical understanding of the observed elasticity of the basal body.
source: A higher-resolution structure of the membrane domains of the secretins in combination with further molecular simulations may allow a full mechanical understanding of the observed elasticity of the basal body.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: The isolated S. flexneri injectisome has a slightly larger diameter than in situ structures.
source: Further, the isolated S. flexneri injectisome has a slightly larger diameter.
evidence: This is observed from comparison of structures.

claim: The 24-meric YscD assembly is compatible with the basal body's diameter, as observed by cryo-EM.
source: In particular, the 24-meric YscD assembly is compatible with the basal body's diameter, as observed by cryo-EM, while a higher number of YscD units would lead to a poorer match with the experimental data.
evidence: This is determined by fitting models to the cryo-EM density.

claim: The ring model for the TM and cytosolic domain of YscD further confirms a 24-mer stoichiometry.
source: Moreover, the ring model for the TM and cytosolic domain of YscD further confirms a 24-mer stoichiometry as observed from the optimal fit with the cryo-EM density.
evidence: This is determined by fitting models to the cryo-EM density.

claim: The model constructed of 24 YscJ molecules does not produce gaps or overlaps in the final structural assembly.
source: Taking the observed stoichiometry of EscJ into account (Crepin et al., 2005; Yip et al., 2005), the model constructed of 24 YscJ molecules does not produce gaps or overlaps in the final structural assembly, as we otherwise obtained when using a higher or lower stoichiometry.
evidence: This is determined from computational modeling.

claim: The outer diameter of the assembled YscJ 24-meric ring matched well the inner diameter of a YscD 24-meric ring.
source: Moreover, while we cannot rule out a different ring arrangement for YscJ in Yersinia compared to EscJ in E.coli, the outer diameter of the assembled YscJ 24-meric ring matched well the inner diameter of a YscD 24-meric ring.
evidence: This is determined from computational modeling.

claim: The short loop linking the TM helix and first periplasmic domain does not allow for large flexibility, providing a solid anchor point for the first YscD periplasmic domain at the membrane surface.
source: The short loop linking the two domains does not allow for large flexibility, providing a solid anchor point for the first YscD periplasmic domain at the membrane surface, and forcing a preferential perpendicular orientation to the IM.
evidence: This is determined from MD simulations of the TM domain.

claim: MD simulations suggested a limited fluctuation for the TM portion of YscD embedded in a membrane model.
source: MD simulations also suggested a limited fluctuation for this portion of YscD embedded in a membrane model, confirming the preferential orientation found in the 24-mer YscD ring assembly (Figure 4).
evidence: This is determined from MD simulations.

claim: The cryo-ET density could be optimally fitted only by extended forms similar to the X-ray YscD conformation.
source: Although the cryo-ET density could be optimally fitted only by extended forms similar to the X-ray YscD conformation, MD snapshots of individual monomers in more compact forms (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) allowed the construction, without incurring in steric clashes, of YscD 24-mer ring structures representative of possible states of intermediate compression compared to the fully extended ring model.
evidence: This is determined by fitting models to the cryo-ET density.

claim: Bacteria are likely exposed to considerable physical forces in vivo, originating from swimming motions, contact with host cells, or from changes in osmolarity of the surrounding medium.
source: Bacteria are likely exposed to considerable physical forces in vivo, originating from swimming motions, contact with host cells, or from changes in osmolarity of the surrounding medium.
evidence: This is based on general knowledge of bacterial physiology.

claim: It would be interesting to quantitatively assess the injectisome's basal body elongation capabilities with biophysical techniques, for example, atomic force microscopy and force spectroscopy.
